chunks: as Jesus, son of Mary, had said to the disciples:
"Who will help me in the way of God?"
and they had answered: "We are the helpers of God."
Then a section among the children of Israel believed, but a section among them did not.
So We helped those who believed against their enemies, and they prevailed over them.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the disciples of Jesus being called 'helpers of God' in this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the paradigm of 'Ansar Allah' (God's supporters), linking the believers' duty to the historical precedent of Isa's disciples (Al-Hawariyyun) who embodied steadfastness. It highlights the dichotomy within the Children of Israel, where divine support was granted specifically to the faction that remained faithful, serving as a model for the Shia community's role in upholding divine truth against opposition.
